content:
sanjay: quick heads-up — ran a focused profiling run on Llama-15B-v2 across AWQ/INT8/FP8 paths. observed strange p99 spikes tied to head-KV dim mismatches when RoPE scaling > 1.15. attaching trace dump and notes.

maya: ugh. is this the same regression we saw after the kernel selector change last week? :thinking_face:

sanjay: similar symptom but different hotspot. last week was kernel fallback due to stride mismatch; this one is microbatching + KV stride causing cache thrash on the headwise kernels.
alex: can you paste the perf counters / top stacks?
sanjay: paste below — took a 10k req sample with 8-token avg seq, bursty 4->64 microbatching.
```
# perf summary (AWQ int8 run, RoPE scale 1.2)
total tokens: 1,240,000
served on gpu0/gpu1
p50: 21ms p95: 82ms p99: 240ms
kernel_fallback_rate: 6.7% (was 0.8% baseline)
kv-cache-evicts/sec: 42
head-kv-hit-ratio: 0.72 -> drops to 0.45 on scale>1.15
hot-kernel: matmul_headwise_quant_int8 (fallback to generic_matmul when mismatch)
```

maya: interesting — fallback to generic_matmul explains CPU path on some batches. any trace showing which requests trigger it?
sanjay: yes — mostly long-context few-shot prompts with RoPE-expanded positions (calibration prompts in the batch). when RoPE scale applied it shifts implicit pos indexes -> head rotations exceed precomputed tiled layout so kernel selector picks generic path.
tara: is this only for AWQ int8 or also FP8/gptq artifacts?
sanjay: reproduced across AWQ and GPTQ int8. FP8 path less affected because we use different kernel with dynamic tiling that tolerates stride.
ci-bot: perf/regression-checker — created perf issue #RFC-1273 for head-KV-rope-slew on 2165556789

alex: short-term mitigation ideas?
maya: we could force the optimized headwise kernel when RoPE scale within [0.9,1.3] and fall back only if explicit stride incompat. basically relax selector for known-safe cases.
tara: maybe add a KV-prefetch alignment stage during microbatch assemble to ensure contiguous layout across requests. cheaper than changing kernels.
sanjay: tried forcing selector locally — p99 goes down from 240ms -> 95ms, fallback_rate -> 1.1%. accuracy delta ~ -0.2% on calibration set (small).

sanjay: calibration details: ran on 150 calibration prompts (mix of instruction, few-shot, long-dialog). metric is exact-match-ish scoring on canonical outputs. numbers:
```
AWQ-int8 baseline (no force): accuracy 0.912
AWQ-int8 force-head-kernel: 0.910
GPTQ-int8 baseline: 0.914
GPTQ-int8 force-head-kernel: 0.913
FP8 baseline: 0.915
```

maya: -0.2% is acceptable if it buys 2.5x p99 improvement in prod. ops?
tara: long-term we should tweak the kernel selector to be aware of RoPE scaling transforms and prefer specialized kernels when pos-map is predictable. also consider adding a tiny precompute step to normalize pos indexes for the fast path.

alex: could we instead change batching heuristics — e.g., disallow mixing RoPE-scaled and non-scaled requests in same microbatch? seems like the combinatorics cause layout mismatch.
sanjay: yep. single-variant microbatches reduce fallback to 0.4% but increases avg latency by ~6% due to smaller microbatching efficiency. tradeoff.

ops-bot: deployment note — rolling canary started on dedicated pool redwood-ded-02 with forced head-kernel off by default. monitor p99 and model accuracy.

maya: action items:
- (sanjay) open PR to relax kernel selector thresholds w/ feature flag (force_head_kernel_rope_relax). link tests + perf harness.
- (alex) add microbatch isolation toggle in batcher config per route.
- (tara) prototype KV-prefetch aligner to coalesce head-kv slices pre-batch.
- (maya) run extended calibration (1k prompts) to measure worst-case accuracy delta across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8.

sanjay: creating issue for PR + attaching minimal repro. repro command below:
```
# repro (docker image: redwood/runtime-profiler:canary)
python -m perf.repro --model llm-llama-15b-v2 --quant awq_int8 --rope-scale 1.2 \
  --batch-config microbatch=8,max_batch=64 --calib-set ./calib/rope_longshot.json --out /tmp/trace.json
```

alex: please add a flamegraph and `nvprof --csv` snippet to the issue. I'll look at kernel-level memory access patterns.
tara: one more note — we saw head dimension variations (head_kv_dim 64 vs 80) exacerbate misalignment. catalog shows models with non-power-of-two head dims hit this more. add that to heuristics.

sanjay: good call. attaching quick table from run:
```
# small table
head_kv_dim | fallback_rate | p99
64          | 6.7%          | 240ms
80          | 11.3%         | 310ms
96          | 4.2%          | 180ms
```

maya: 80 looks worst — maybe stride math with 80 crosses tile boundary. add rule: if head_kv_dim % tile != 0, prefer conservative layout or align copies.
sanjay: noted. I'll push a draft PR and link the perf issue. want to avoid immediate global rollback since hosted traffic is still fine. plan: canary + enable force-head-kernel for routes with p99>150ms.
tara: ok — ping me on PR. also queue an eval run for FP8 to ensure no surprise bias.
alex: cool. thanks for the trace, sanjay. this one felt subtle but actionable. :rocket:
